overview: The Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee reviewed preliminary financial modeling for city-wide capital projects and projected property tax impacts of various debt exclusion levels. The committee also analyzed updated cost estimates for specific site options and a 50-year life cycle cost study of proposed HVAC systems.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from the previous meeting with one minor name correction.

items.title: Project and MSBA Updates
items.summary: Chairman Graham reported that the MSBA confirmed the project is not in violation of regulations following the removal of site Option D and discussed the MSBA request to explore a 9-12 only enrollment option for comparison purposes.

items.title: City Capital Projects and Cost Impact Presentation
items.summary: City officials presented a broad overview of Medford’s $900 million capital project needs, modeling the potential tax impacts of debt exclusions ranging from $440 million to $607 million for different residential and commercial property types.

items.title: Discussion of City Financial Data
items.summary: Committee members and residents discussed the financial presentation, with several participants questioning the framing of city debt against school needs and requesting more data on revenue growth and the educational vision for the project.

items.title: PSR Cost Estimates and MSBA Reimbursement
items.summary: The project team presented refined cost estimates for the C2.2a and C3.4a options and clarified that the project's effective MSBA reimbursement rate will likely increase as incentive points are finalized during schematic design.

items.title: Project Timeline Update
items.summary: The committee reviewed the schedule leading up to a preferred option selection on June 10 and the subsequent Preferred Schematic Report submission on June 25.

items.title: Evaluation Criteria Matrix and Life Cycle Cost Analysis
items.summary: Sustainability consultants presented a 50-year life cycle cost analysis comparing geothermal and air-to-water heat pump systems, finding that while geothermal is more efficient, it currently carries a $28 million incremental upfront cost.
